steps.en: What you see: The image mirrors the parasternal long axis, with the left ventricle, septum above, posterior wall below, mitral valve behind and aortic root in front. The ascending aorta runs further than in any other apical view.
Landmarks to confirm: Do not accept the view until each of these is on screen.
Common mistakes and how to correct them: Each mistake below comes from the view catalogue with its correction.
Normal values and stenosis thresholds: Peak aortic velocity 4 m per s or above means severe stenosis.
Mean transaortic gradient 40 mmHg or above means severe stenosis.
Measure the aortic root at end diastole with the leading edge to leading edge method.

Pitfalls: Wall labels flip if rotation is wrong, so confirm the aorta is anterior before naming ischaemic territories. This view understates aortic root diameter compared with the long axis, so measure the root there.

spot.en: Landmarks to confirm: Cavity of left ventricle
Common mistakes and how to correct them: Losing the aortic valve by over rotation toward two chamber. Correct it by rotating back a touch until both aortic cusps reappear.
Foreshortened outflow that hides coaptation. Correct it by sliding to the true apex and lengthening the ventricle before judging the valve.
Septum vertical from wrong rotation so walls misassign. Correct it by rotating until the septum lies near horizontal with the aorta anterior.

todo.en: How to get it: Place the probe at apex, fifth intercostal space, rotated about one hundred twenty degrees from four chamber.
Point the probe marker toward the left, about three o clock.
Keep rotating from the two chamber to about one hundred twenty degrees until the aorta opens. Assign walls only after the septum lies near horizontal as in the long axis.
Freeze the image only when every listed landmark is on screen at once.

remember.en: Take high aortic velocities from an apical line.

q.en: The three chamber mirrors which view?

why.en: Cavity, septum, mitral valve and aorta line up as in the long axis.

q.en: Which walls does the three chamber show?

why.en: Rotation to one hundred twenty degrees faces the anteroseptal and inferolateral walls.

q.en: Where should root diameter be measured?

why.en: The long axis gives the largest true root diameter for surveillance.
